issues.description: Check name inconsistent between PR description ('compute_image_publicly_shared') and shipped artifacts ('compute_image_not_publicly_shared')
issues.detail: The PR title, CHANGELOG, file paths, and class name all use 'compute_image_not_publicly_shared', but the PR description references 'compute_image_publicly_shared'. The check name is the contract identifier callers and dashboards bind to. Pick one name and propagate it everywhere before merge.

issues.description: IAM-policy fetch failure silently degrades to publicly_shared=False, producing PASS on auth errors
issues.detail: In _get_images, if getIamPolicy raises (e.g., permission denied, as test-image-3 simulates), the image is appended with publicly_shared=False and the check reports PASS. The postcondition 'PASS means verified non-public' is violated: verification failure looks like a clean bill of health. Introduce an explicit unknown/MANUAL state or surface an error finding.

issues.description: Image listing is not threaded via __threading_call__ like every other resource in compute_service.py
issues.detail: Every other collection in compute_service.py uses __threading_call__ over projects/regions/zones. _get_images iterates project_ids serially in the constructor, inconsistent with the surrounding module conventions. Match the existing style or document a specific technical reason not to.

issues.description: Service test pins the leaky behavior by asserting publicly_shared=False on the IAM-policy exception path
issues.detail: The test for test-image-3 conflates two reasons for False — truly not shared, or policy fetch failed. This masks the failure mode and pins the current leaky contract, making future correction a test-breaking change. The test should assert an unknown/error state, not coerce auth failures into PASS.

issues.description: Image ADT under-specifies invariants: missing bindings context and self_link/URI common to other compute models
issues.detail: The Image model carries only a derived publicly_shared boolean plus name/id/project_id, dropping the public members/bindings that justify the boolean and the self_link/URI other compute ADTs carry. Remediation and audit consumers frequently need 'why' alongside 'whether', and consistent identity fields reduce surprise for downstream reporting.

synthesis.summary: The new check does one thing cleanly, but two contract-level issues need fixing before merge. The check name disagrees between the PR description and the shipped artifacts — the identifier callers bind to must be stated once. More substantively, IAM-policy fetch failures are silently coerced into publicly_shared=False, so auth errors look like a clean PASS and the test pins this leaky behavior. Listing also bypasses the module's __threading_call__ convention, and the Image ADT is thin on identity and binding context. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK on the failure path and the name; ADT consistency is a follow-up.
